summary: This paper introduces electron pair interferometry (EPI), a measurement protocol for nuclear spin qubits in silicon quantum dots that uses shuttled electron pairs to read out parity via singlet/triplet interference, enabling a complete gate set for universal quantum computation tailored to CSS quantum error correction. The approach maintains robustness to charge noise and demonstrates controlled sensitivity to magnetic field inhomogeneities, leveraging recent advances in isotopically enriched silicon (single-digit ppm $^{29}$Si), large quantum dot arrays, and coherent electron shuttling.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer extremely long coherence times but are difficult to control and measure directly; the hyperfine interaction with shuttled electrons provides a scalable path to entanglement, but a measurement protocol robust to the noise environment of this platform was lacking.
method: Electrons are initialized into a singlet state, split and adiabatically shuttled along distinct paths through a quantum dot array to visit complementary subsets of isoelectronic nuclear spin qubits via hyperfine CPhase operations, accumulating a phase $\phi(t_M)$ dependent on nuclear parity; recombination and singlet/triplet measurement via spin-to-charge conversion yields parity readout with $P_S = \cos^2(\phi(t_M)/2)$. Global NMR and selective hyperfine $Z_\pi$ rotations complete the gate set.
result: EPI achieves parity measurements sensitive only to the magnitude of magnetic field differences (not sign), showing very low sensitivity to charge noise and tunable sensitivity to DC/AC magnetic field inhomogeneity depending on their relative strengths, with the architecture compatible with error rates below $10^{-3}$ when $^{29}$Si backgrounds are reduced to $\lesssim 50$ ppm.
